Step 1 - Load 1 to 4 reference images. Q21 does not seem to like character sheets as well as I thought, so my recommendation is to go with 4. Just make sure you wire in the load image nodes as needed. Adjust the input switch Prompt Subgraph

Step 2 - Make any adjustments you want using the customize section. This is purely optional. It will work fine without it. It's broken out into sections if you want to fine tune certain parts of the body but don't want it showing up in the other angles. 

Step 3 - Adjust settings as desired. I've done most of my tests with turbo for  the sake speed. 

Step 4 - Set output folder and save name.

Step 5 - Hit run

Differences from previous versions: 

This relies heavily on multi-line indexes and switches. That does make this version less customizable than before. It also has math operations in place so you do not need to resset the index after each run. This one also includes more varied backgrounds and will put the character in different settings. I don't think that's entirely necessary, but people seem to like it.

Best practices: 


You can adjust outfits and accessories in the Master Prompt, but I think you're better off making a  new reference sheet with those changes instead of hoping all 30 outputs are consistent. Obviously adding in a third reference image with that adjustment will help. 

In theory you could add different backgrounds and settings in the Angle Prompt section. I chose a more neutral approach because that has tended to work best for me when training character loras.
